for_loop.quote: Each pass starts by setting i = 1 again
for_loop.rule: wrong rule: The initialization of a for loop runs again after a pass of the body. Right rule: The initialization runs exactly once, before the first condition test.

increment_operators.quote: Then i++ runs before the body and adds 2; so i is 3
increment_operators.rule: wrong rule: i++ increases i by 2. Right rule: i++ (and ++i) increases i by exactly 1.

loop_control.quote: Then i++ runs before the body and adds 2; so i is 3; So every pass prints the same thing, 3
loop_control.rule: wrong rule: The update part of a for header (e.g. i = i - 4) runs before the body on each pass, so the first pass already sees the updated value. Right rule: The update runs after the body, before the next condition test; the first pass uses the initial value.
